title: Replace a foil shaver’s cutter and foil
instruction: Remove the worn foil and cutter. Fit the new cutter and foil, briefly run the shaver to check the assembly, then switch it off.
context: Replacing a worn cutter and foil restores a reusable appliance. The hands must handle two distinct parts and check the assembled head under power.
setup: A 147 mm moulded shaver lies switch-up in a 110 × 170 mm rubber cradle on a 400 × 400 mm mat. Its 58 × 22 mm steel cutter and 82 × 40 mm domed steel foil start installed at (84, 18) mm. Separate 82 × 52 mm plastic trays hold a compatible cutter at (158, −84) mm and foil at (166, 126) mm. Empty discard trays sit at (3, −135) and (10, 140) mm. The power switch at (80, −46) mm and its indicator face up. Power starts off.
scoring: Milestones are sequential. 0.25 when both old parts are released in their discard trays, within 26 mm horizontally and 9 mm vertically of their reference centres. 0.50 when the new cutter is also within 6 mm on each axis of its seat with absolute long-axis and positive up-axis dot products above 0.97. 0.75 when the new foil is also released, within 5.5 mm on each horizontal axis and 6 mm vertically of its seat, with the same orientation bounds and both tabs within 6.5 mm crosswise and vertically. 1.00 after at least 0.35 s powered with both replacements seated and at least 1 mm of cutter travel, with power off at the end. Powering with neither foil registered gives 0.00.
reset_notes: Reset power off, put both old parts in the head, return the new parts to their stock trays and empty the discard trays.
fidelity: Two loose steel parts, spring-loaded foil registration and a motor-driven cutter are simulated with simplified contact shapes. The stainless through-holes are render geometry. Bounded spring forces represent the locating faces, drive and supported two-finger grasp.
